l5-6-A_data_cleaning.title: Before and after data cleaning
l5-6-A_data_cleaning.caption: Eight synthetic raw records become six accepted transactions. The exact duplicate is removed, negative quantity quarantined, missing quantity imputed to 3 with its indicator retained, and the verified 50,000 USD sale kept.
l5-6-A_data_cleaning.alt: Before table flags duplicate row 8, missing quantity in row 3, North spelling in row 2, and negative quantity in row 4. Clean table retains six transactions and a True missing flag for S03; the decision log explains each choice.
l5-6-A_data_cleaning.question: Why is S06 retained despite its unusually large revenue?
l5-6-A_data_cleaning.answer: Its quantity and price were verified as valid. A statistical extreme alone is not an error.

l5-6-B_missingness_mechanisms.title: MCAR, MAR and MNAR income reporting
l5-6-B_missingness_mechanisms.caption: Illustrative patient-income mechanisms, not diagnoses. MCAR is random loss independent of age/income; MAR depends on observed age and not income conditional on age; MNAR still depends on unreported income after conditioning.
l5-6-B_missingness_mechanisms.alt: Three reporting diagrams: random loss causes missing income; observed age predicts reporting under MAR; true unreported income predicts reporting under MNAR even after observed age is accounted for. A heatmap cannot prove MAR versus MNAR.
l5-6-B_missingness_mechanisms.question: Does missingness varying by age prove MAR?
l5-6-B_missingness_mechanisms.answer: No. It can contradict MCAR, but MNAR may remain possible because unreported income is unobserved.

l5-6-C_mean_median_boxplot.title: Mean, median, fences and whiskers
l5-6-C_mean_median_boxplot.caption: Exact synthetic values: [10,12,13,14,15], then append 100. Mean changes from 12.8 to 82/3; median from 13 to 13.5. Quartiles use linear percentiles; the fence thresholds are not whisker endpoints.
l5-6-C_mean_median_boxplot.alt: Mean/median comparison shows mean 12.8 then 27.3333 and median 13 then 13.5. Augmented boxplot has Q1 12.25, Q3 14.75, fences 8.5/18.5, actual whiskers 10/15, and outlier 100.
l5-6-C_mean_median_boxplot.question: Does the upper whisker end at 18.5?
l5-6-C_mean_median_boxplot.answer: No. 18.5 is the upper fence; the whisker ends at the largest observed value inside it, 15.

l7-8-A_transformations.title: Scaling and transforming the same values
l7-8-A_transformations.caption: Exact values [10,20,30,40,100]. Min–max uses 10 and 100; standardization uses mean 40 and population SD 10√10 (ddof=0); log1p uses natural logarithms. Decimals are rounded to six places beside exact expressions.
l7-8-A_transformations.alt: Table maps five original values to exact min–max fractions, standardized multiples of 1/√10 and natural logs of x+1. Aligned dot plots show standardization preserves relative spacing and distribution shape.
l7-8-A_transformations.question: Does standardization make the data normally distributed?
l7-8-A_transformations.answer: No. It shifts and rescales values using a positive affine transformation, preserving shape.

l7-8-B_unseen_minmax.title: An unseen scaled value can exceed one
l7-8-B_unseen_minmax.caption: Fit min–max on training values from 10 to 100, then transform 120 unchanged. The result is (120−10)/90 = 11/9, approximately 1.222222. Clipping is disabled.
l7-8-B_unseen_minmax.alt: Training minimum 10 and maximum 100 define (x−10)/90. An arrow applies this fixed formula to unseen x=120, yielding 11/9 greater than one; refitting on test values is marked leakage.
l7-8-B_unseen_minmax.question: Should the scaler be refitted to force 120 into the unit interval?
l7-8-B_unseen_minmax.answer: No. Preserve the training-fitted parameters. Optional clipping hides the extent beyond the fitted range.

l7-8-C_encoding.title: Ordered severity and unordered regions
l7-8-C_encoding.caption: Severity explicitly maps Low < Medium < High to 0,1,2. Region membership is represented by four one-hot columns. Ordinal rank does not establish equal distances between severity levels.
l7-8-C_encoding.alt: Two connected tables encode Low/Medium/High as 0/1/2 and North/South/East/West as one-hot membership rows. Arbitrary region integers can introduce an unintended order or distance.
l7-8-C_encoding.question: Why can North=0, South=1, East=2, West=3 be misleading?
l7-8-C_encoding.answer: A model may interpret numerical order or distance although the regions are unordered.

l7-8-D_feature_engineering.title: A transaction becomes useful features
l7-8-D_feature_engineering.caption: Synthetic transaction: quantity 3, price 200 USD/unit, discount 0.10, cost 120 USD/unit; assumed date 2024-01-08. Gross 600 USD, net 540, cost 360, profit 180, margin 1/3; month 1 and weekday 0 (Monday).
l7-8-D_feature_engineering.alt: Raw-field table points to formula/result table computing revenue, cost, profit, margin and date features. A caution excludes final profit, future sales and later returns from earlier predictions.
l7-8-D_feature_engineering.question: Can final realized profit predict an outcome before the sale is complete?
l7-8-D_feature_engineering.answer: Only if it was actually available at that prediction time; otherwise it is a future-derived leakage feature.

l9-10-A_split_comparison.title: Choose a split for the data structure
l9-10-A_split_comparison.caption: Synthetic 12-record schematics use nine training and three test records. Random suits independent records; stratification approximates class proportions; grouping isolates patients; chronological splitting holds out later dates.
l9-10-A_split_comparison.alt: Four labeled split patterns: random record assignment, class-proportion preserving assignment, all three records of patient P4 held out, and October–December held out after January–September training. Color and hatching identify partitions.
l9-10-A_split_comparison.question: Does stratification prevent repeated-patient leakage?
l9-10-A_split_comparison.answer: No. Group splitting is needed to keep a patient entirely in one partition.

l9-10-B_safe_workflow.title: A safe predictive workflow
l9-10-B_safe_workflow.caption: Split first. During tuning, fit preprocessing within each training fold; transform its validation fold separately. Select the recipe, refit on all training data, transform test with training-fitted preprocessing and evaluate once.
l9-10-B_safe_workflow.alt: Training-side validation loop selects preprocessing/model settings before final refitting. Test remains untouched until final transformation/evaluation. Red dashed arrows mark test-data fitting and future-derived features as leakage.
l9-10-B_safe_workflow.question: When must a scaler be fitted during cross-validation?
l9-10-B_safe_workflow.answer: Inside each fold using only that fold’s training partition; final refitting uses all training data after recipe selection.

l9-10-C_regression_capacity.title: Underfitting, appropriate capacity and overfitting
l9-10-C_regression_capacity.caption: Reproducible synthetic regression, seed 42: y=0.7x²−0.5x+1 plus noise SD 0.65. Prespecified polynomial degrees 1,2,15 share 24 training observations and 400 independent held-out observations. MSE values are calculated; extreme curve segments outside the stated axis are clipped.
l9-10-C_regression_capacity.alt: Three panels show identical training points with linear, quadratic and degree-15 polynomial fits. Training MSE: 4.3248, 0.2815, 0.0829; held-out MSE: 4.1442, 0.4425, 0.6539. The quadratic generalizes best in this stated example.
l9-10-C_regression_capacity.question: Why is the smallest training error not the strongest evidence of generalization?
l9-10-C_regression_capacity.answer: A flexible model can fit training noise. Here degree 15 reduces training MSE but has larger held-out MSE than degree 2.
